ai.title: Supabase CPC experiment separates ads surface from execution surface
ai.summary: The Supabase CPC experiment now models two distinct surface concepts: an ad-request surface (`cli_chat`) and a local-execution surface (`desktop_macos`, `desktop_linux`). A new resolver, `resolveSupabaseCpcDeliverySurfaces`, validates that both surfaces are present and qualified, returning `ad_surface_mismatch` or `surface_mismatch` when they are not. `evaluateSupabaseFormatCpcEligibility` now checks the execution surface through `isSupabaseFormatCpcExecutionSurface`, and both arms of `SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_ARM_REACH` reference the shared `SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_EXECUTION_SURFACES` constant so the execution surface list is defined in one place.
ai.evidence: common/src/ads/supabase-format-cpc-experiment.ts: added SUPABASE_CPC_AD_SURFACE ('cli_chat'), SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_EXECUTION_SURFACES (['desktop_macos','desktop_linux']), type guards isSupabaseCpcAdSurface / isSupabaseFormatCpcExecutionSurface, resolver resolveSupabaseCpcDeliverySurfaces, and rewired SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_ARM_REACH display/agentic executionSurfaces to reference SUPABASE_FORMAT_CPC_EXECUTION_SURFACES; evaluateSupabaseFormatCpcEligibility now gates via isSupabaseFormatCpcExecutionSurface instead of raw string check.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show who consumes resolveSupabaseCpcDeliverySurfaces or when the new surface split is rolled out to live traffic.

ai.title: Remove Freebuff refund display and end-session refund wording
ai.summary: The Freebuff landing screen no longer shows pending or completed Freebucks refunds: cli/src/app.tsx and cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx dropped `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from the session store destructure, the `AuthedSurfaceProps` and `FreebuffLandingScreenProps` types, and the two refund text spans that read from them. The `/end-session` slash command in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts likewise lost its 'get 90% of unspent cost back, rounded down' description, now reading just 'End your current session'. No replacement UI or command is wired up in this diff, so the refund flow is effectively disabled from the Freebuff surfaces for now.

ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the store side of `useFreebuffSession`, so whether `lastRefund`/`refundPending` still exist upstream or were removed there is not visible, and there is no note about where the refund UI is moving.

ai.title: Remove automatic provider stop sequence from agent stream
ai.summary: The `globalStopSequence` constant, which was derived from `endsAgentStepParam` and passed as a `stopSequences` entry into the AI SDK stream parameters, has been removed from both `constants.ts` and `prompt-agent-stream.ts`. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts`, the import { globalStopSequence } from './constants' line was removed and the `stopSequences: [globalStopSequence]` entry was deleted from the `aiSdkStreamParams` object literal.

facts: A selected connection, or BYOK setup opened from a Freebuff wall, reaches the chat without a Freebuff session.

Entry from a Freebuff wall (Freebucks spent, daily cap reached). Those screens have no input, so without this a user who ran out could never type `/byok` — the one route that does not need Freebucks at all.
BYOK setup opened from a Freebuff wall holds no session, so a prompt has nowhere to run until a connection is selected. Keep the text in the input rather than consuming it.
Out of Freebucks on the picker: every row's Enter opens plans, so BYOK is the one way to keep working today.
During BYOK setup there is no session to end; marking it would swap the setup chat for the session-ended banner.
True when the chat may be shown without a Freebuff session: a connection is selected, or the user is setting one up.

ai.title: BYOK setup opens from Freebuff walls without a session
ai.summary: A new BYOK setup state was added to the CLI so users who hit a Freebucks wall can start a `/byok` session without a live Freebuff session, since those landing screens have no input. `cli/src/utils/byok.ts` adds a `setupOpen` flag with `openByokSetup`, `closeByokSetup`, `isByokSetupOpen`, and `useBypassesFreebuffSession`, and `cli/src/commands/byok.ts` `enterByokSetup()` posts the BYOK usage guidance and opens setup. `cli/src/commands/router.ts` `routeUserPrompt` now queues non-command input until a connection is selected, and `cli/src/app.tsx` `AuthedSurfaceRoutes` uses `useBypassesFreebuffSession` so a selected connection or active setup bypasses the session-required routing. On the picker, `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` renders a `ByokWallOffer` (press B) when `freebucksCannotAffordAnyModel` is true, and `/byok off` closes setup only when nothing is selected.
ai.evidence: cli/src/utils/byok.ts: added setupOpen flag and openByokSetup/closeByokSetup/isByokSetupOpen/useBypassesFreebuffSession exports; cli/src/commands/byok.ts enterByokSetup() pushes the BYOK usage system message and calls openByokSetup(); cli/src/commands/router.ts routeUserPrompt now holds non-command prompts while setup is open; cli/src/app.tsx AuthedSurfaceRoutes uses useBypassesFreebuffSession instead of checking selected !== undefined.
ai.unknowns: The consumer of `isByokSetupOpen` in `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts` and the exact landing-screen states where the offer is rendered beyond the picker are not fully shown.

facts: MiMo 2.6 Pro (2026-09-21). NEW ids rather than the retired `base2-free-mimo-pro`: released builds from before 2026-08-04 still bundle that id pinned to MiMo 2.5 Pro, and reusing it would make those requests look like this model's traffic in every per-agent query.
Pinned to its one model like every root: a root that allowed both MiMo ids would sell the 50-Freebuck Pro through the 10-Freebuck Flash session.

MiMo 2.6 Pro (2026-09-21), plan-only at limited access, 50 Freebucks. Unlike the MiMo row above it has its own id: it is a different, dearer model, and one wire id per entitlement is the rule (a Pro served under the Flash id would be a 50-Freebuck model sold at 10).

MiMo 2.6 Flash since 2026-09-21, under the unchanged wire id (see FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID). Same Xiaomi rate card as 2.5 to the cent ($0.14 in / $0.28 out / $0.0028 cache read per M), so nothing about this row's economics or its unmetered/fallback role moved with the name.
Restore it together with Flash leaving FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS, not before: the argument returns only when Flash is free again.
NEW because the model under this row changed (2.5 -> 2.6 Flash) while its id did not — exactly the returning user the badge exists for.

ai.title: MiMo 2.6 Flash and MiMo 2.6 Pro join the free model picker
ai.summary: MiMo 2.5 is replaced in the free model picker by MiMo 2.6 Flash (same `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID` wire id), and a separate MiMo 2.6 Pro row is added under the new `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID`, carrying its own 50-Freebuck entitlement so a root cannot sell the dearest model through the unmetered 10-Freebuck Flash session. MiMo 2.6 Pro is full-access only, marked `isNew` and `limited` at limited access, and ships with a `priceWarning` because its Freebucks price is a launch estimate from Xiaomi's rate card. The picker surfaces that caveat as a warning-coloured 'Price subject to change' chip, and three dedicated roots (base2, base3, reviewer) are introduced so each surface runs the model under its own id instead of collapsing it onto the Flash root.
ai.evidence: README.md and README.zh-CN.md swap the 'MiMo 2.5' picker row for 'MiMo 2.6 Flash' and add a 'MiMo 2.6 Pro' row; common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID` and the `MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL` row, and adds `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_PRICE_WARNING`; agents/base2/base2-free-mimo-2-6-pro.ts, agents/base3-free-mimo-2-6-pro.ts and agents/reviewer/code-reviewer-mimo-2-6-pro.ts are new files wired to `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V26_PRO_MODEL_ID`; common/src/constants/free-agents.ts registers 'base2-free-mimo-2-6-pro', 'base3-free-mimo-2-6-pro' and 'code-reviewer-mimo-2-6-pro' under that id; common/src/constants/model-config.ts adds the `mimoV26Pro` wire id; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx renders `model.priceWarning` as a warning chip.
ai.migration: No action required. Sessions already running on the MiMo row keep their model because `FREEBUFF_MIMO_V25_MODEL_ID` still serves MiMo 2.6 Flash; saved picker selections are not rewritten since the id is unchanged. Existing root-agent allowlists that referenced 'base2-free-mimo-pro' are unaffected, as that id was already retired before this commit.
